YEAR BOOK OF THE YOUNG MEN'S CHRISTIAN ASSOCIATIONS OF NORTH AMERICA, FOR THE YEAR 1898
Internet Archive: ymcayearbookand00assogoog — NOT lending-restricted, djvu text 2,301,751 bytes

FIVE ANNUAL VOLUMES ARE BOUND IN THIS ONE SCAN. THE CATALOGUE CALLS IT 1896.
---------------------------------------------------------------------------
Each carries its own title page, in the same setting: "NORTH AMERICA, / For the Year XXXX, /
PRICE FIFTY CENTS."

    scan line     259   For the Year 1896
    scan line  31,596   For the Year 1897
    scan line  73,986   For the Year 1898   <- A YEAR THIS PROJECT DID NOT HOLD
    scan line 114,510   For the Year 1899
    scan line 165,312   For the Year 1900

The Internet Archive record gives `year: 1896` and nothing else. Four of the five volumes are
invisible to the catalogue. This is the second scan in two hours found to hold more volumes than
its record admits — `yearbookyoungme01commgoog` holds 1899 and 1900 and is catalogued 1899 — so
in this series it should be assumed rather than hoped for: SCAN THE WHOLE TEXT FOR TITLE PAGES
BEFORE DECIDING WHAT AN ITEM CONTAINS.

A signature that separates a title page from a statistics heading, since both read "FOR THE YEAR
XXXX": a title page sits under "NORTH AMERICA," and above "PRICE FIFTY CENTS"; a statistics
heading names the PREVIOUS year and sits under a line about American associations. In this item
line 114,878 reads "FROM / American Young Men's Christian Associations, / FOR THE YEAR 1898" —
that is the 1899 volume's statistics table, not a sixth volume.


I. THE MONTREAL ASSOCIATION'S PAID STAFF, 1898
==============================================
The Quebec branch directory, scan line 81,551, quoted with the OCR's slips left where they fall:

    Quebec.
    Montreal                         D  A.  Badge
        Asst.,                       C.  K.  Calhoun
        Asst.,                       Archibald  McKeUar
        Phys.  Director,             W.  H.  Ball.  Jr.
        Asst.  Phys.  Director,      C.  B.  Powter
    McGill  University               A.  H.  Grace
    Quebec                           H.  H.  Distin
    Sherbrooke                       J.  H.  Bryce

That is:

    General Secretary            D. A. BUDGE
    Assistant                    C. K. CALHOUN
    Assistant                    ARCHIBALD McKELLAR
    Physical Director            W. H. BALL, JR.
    Assistant Physical Director  C. B. POWTER
    (McGill University)          A. H. GRACE

This volume carries no alphabetical list with entry years — that feature appears in the 1899
volume. So no dates of entry are available for 1898; the branch directory is all there is, and it
is enough.


II. WHY THIS ONE ROSTER IS WORTH THE WHOLE SEARCH
=================================================
The YMCA of Montreal's annual report for the year ending 30 April 1899 gives the Permanent Camp
Committee's own account of the 1898 season, and this project has it (f_4911, f_4913): "The camp
was under the charge of the following: Messrs. A. MacKellar, C. B. Powter, A. R. Ross, and W. H.
Ball." Four men, and until today the first of them was two letters and a surname.

HE IS ARCHIBALD McKELLAR, AND HE WAS AN ASSISTANT SECRETARY OF THE MONTREAL YMCA.

And the join is tighter than a name. HE APPEARS IN EXACTLY ONE OF THE FIVE VOLUMES IN THIS SCAN.
A search across all five for every plausible spelling — McKellar, MacKellar, McKeUar — returns a
single line, in 1898. He is not on the Montreal staff in 1896, 1897, 1899 or 1900. The one year
he is a paid officer of the association is the one year a document places him in charge of its
camp.

THREE OF THE FOUR MEN who ran the 1898 senior camp are on the association's paid staff in the
same year's volume, in the same eight-line block: McKellar as assistant, Ball as Physical
Director, Powter as his assistant. The fourth, A. R. Ross, is NOT in the directory — consistent
with the pattern this project has already established from nine other volumes (f_4966), that the
camp's people divide into paid officers, who are in the Year Book, and volunteers and seasonal
staff, who systematically are not. Ross is presumably the latter. That is a reading of a pattern,
not a fact about Ross, and it is written as one.

WHAT IT DOES NOT SAY. The volume does not mention the camp. It does not connect McKellar,
Ball or Powter to it. The connection is made entirely by the Montreal annual report, which names
the four men, and this volume supplies only who three of them were in their day jobs — which is
the whole of what it is being used for here.

III. WHAT THE OTHER YEARS IN THIS SCAN ADD
==========================================
1896, 1897, 1899 and 1900 are all years this project already holds from other scans, so they were
not re-read. They are worth knowing about as INDEPENDENT SECOND COPIES: where the 1899 and 1900
readings above rest on `yearbookyoungme01commgoog`, whose 1900 alphabetical list is OCR-ruined,
this scan carries the same two volumes again and may be legible where that one is not. Not
checked. Queued.

IV. "KANAWANA" IN THE 1898 VOLUME
=================================
Zero occurrences, as in every other volume of this series read so far, and for the same reason:
it rosters associations and their paid staff, not their programmes. The camp had been running for
four summers when this volume went to press.

QUERIES RUN AGAINST THE ITEM: a whole-text scan for /FOR (THE )?YEARS? 1[89]dd/ to find the volume
boundaries; 'Montr' in the 1898 volume; 'McKellar|MacKellar|McKeUar' across all five volumes;
'year of entry into' for the alphabetical-list legend (absent from 1898); 'kanawana'.
